# featbit_environment (Resource)

Manages a FeatBit Environment through the documented public API.

Terraform owns the Environment name and description. The parent Project UUID
and Environment key define immutable identity. Updates read the current remote
Environment immediately before mutation so UI-owned settings that are not in
the Terraform schema remain unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "featbit_project" "example" {
  name = "Checkout service"
  key  = "checkout-service"
}

resource "featbit_environment" "example" {
  project_id  = featbit_project.example.id
  name        = "Staging"
  key         = "staging"
  description = "Pre-production validation"
}
```

The reference to `featbit_project.example.id` creates the required dependency;
Terraform therefore creates the Project first and destroys the Environment
first.

## Lifecycle

- `name` and `description` update in place; an omitted description
  canonicalizes to an empty string.
- `project_id` and `key` require replacement.
- Read and destroy resolve the exact UUID within the exact parent Project.
- State is preserved when deletion or an update outcome cannot be confirmed.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Immutable Environment key within the parent Project.
- `name` (String) Environment display name.
- `project_id` (String) Immutable parent Project UUID.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Environment description. An omitted value canonicalizes to an empty string.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Environment UUID.

## Import

Import an Environment with its parent Project UUID and Environment UUID:

```shell
terraform import featbit_environment.example '<project_uuid>/<environment_uuid>'
```

Both components must use 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal UUID form.
